endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Provide input for training materials about the capabilities and limitations of GAI systems related to digital content transparency for AI Actors, other professionals, and the public

endorsements.title: Establishing a Multi-Society Generative AI Task Force Within Radiology
endorsements.quote: Leading public and physician education through social media campaigns and CME courses on GenAI capabilities, limitations, and ethical use.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether health system participation in public or third-party education on generative AI improves understanding of its capabilities, limitations, or risks. Support for this recommendation rests on two endorsements, a federal framework and a radiology society commentary, and no hazard study was supplied to document the scale of misunderstanding.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The two endorsements reflect expert judgment and do not supply outcome data on knowledge, behavior, or harm.

NIST AI 600-1 is a voluntary framework. It asks organizations to provide input for training materials on generative AI capabilities and limitations for AI actors, other professionals, and the public. The radiology task force commentary proposes social media campaigns and CME courses. Neither source creates a binding obligation, and neither cites evaluation data.

commentary.research_gap: No study has measured whether education delivered by health systems changes public, patient, or partner understanding of generative AI risks, or whether any change affects downstream safety or trust. No study has compared formats such as CME courses, social media campaigns, or partner training materials. Baseline studies of how the public and third parties misunderstand generative AI in health care are also absent from the supplied evidence.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice was supplied, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems that adopt this practice have no data on whether education reaches or benefits these groups. Materials may need separate evaluation for language access and readability.
